Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are a community-college student who works night shifts at a package-sorting warehouse to stay enrolled. For over two years you and your fiancé have saved toward a wedding, now five months away. The judge is a financial coach at RIVERBEND COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION, where that savings account is held.

A nonrefundable venue deposit is already paid, and after rent and tuition, $180 a month is all your budget leaves. Your fiancé is the household's primary earner. A term life policy on your fiancé would cost $28 a month, and renter's insurance covering theft, fire and water damage would cost $19 a month.

The laptop your coursework runs on has failed once already. The retailer sells an extended warranty for $299 today or $12 a month for thirty-six months, which totals $432. You also pledged $40 a month to the HARVEST TABLE FOOD PANTRY for a year, and four months of that pledge remain.

The coach (judge) has asked you to decide what the $180 buys. Funding both insurance policies means ending the food pantry pledge early and breaking a commitment you made for a year. Keeping the pledge and taking the $12 a month plan pays $432 instead of $299 and leaves nothing for life insurance.

The coach (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are a financial coach at RIVERBEND COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the student to decide what the $180 a month buys — the term life policy on the fiancé, the renter's insurance, the extended warranty on the laptop, the pledge to the HARVEST TABLE FOOD PANTRY, or some combination of them — and to say plainly what the choice gives up.

During the presentation you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how will this choice look if the laptop never fails again?
If you end the food pantry pledge, what happens the next time you want to give?
